commitResults.messageTitle: Record the submission when grading an assignment
commitResults.messageBody:
Grading an assignment that is not yet submitted is rejected, so a TA
needs a submit and a grade command for every student.

A graded assignment is a submitted one. Let's record the submission
together with the grade, and say so in the feedback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Count weekly listings and clear several students
commitResults.messageBody:
Weekly listings give no totals, so a TA reads every row to check that
nobody was missed. Clear commands take one student, unlike mark and
set, so undoing a batch mark takes one command per student.

Let's show the present, absent and unmarked counts in the attendance
heading and the recorded counts in the participation heading. Let's
also let attendance clear and participation clear repeat id/, clearing
nobody if any ID is unknown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give view specific one-line errors
commitResults.messageBody:
A missing or extra screen name gets a generic five-line format error,
which is cut off in the four-line feedback box.

Let's name the missing screen or the extra text in one line that lists
the valid screens.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat Unicode spaces in saved names as spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
A name in the data file with a non-breaking space, as pasted from a
web page, makes the whole file unreadable, although the same name
typed in a command is accepted.

Let's treat Unicode whitespace as a space when normalizing group,
student and assignment names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report blank parameter values as missing
commitResults.messageBody:
A prefix with no value, such as a/ or s/, is reported as an invalid
value and its rules, although the user typed nothing.

Let's report a blank required value as a missing value with the
command's format, after any wholly missing prefixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep long IDs and group names distinguishable
commitResults.messageBody:
A valid 20-character ID of wide letters is cut off in the Students
table, and long group names that differ only at the end look the same
in the group bar.

Let's widen the ID column within the existing limits and shorten group
names in the middle instead of at the end.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn about likely mistakes in records
commitResults.messageBody:
A positive participation score for an absent student, and assignment
names that differ only in case, spaces or punctuation such as PS1 and
PS-1, are accepted silently, although they are usually typos.

Let's keep accepting them, since they may be intended, but add a
warning to the feedback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix Records selection after assignment changes
commitResults.messageBody: Restrict rename recovery to a valid transition in the same group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep Records in sync through repeated rename undo
commitResults.messageBody: Follow assignment name transitions using group snapshots to retain the correct listing through consecutive undo and redo operations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support late and excused attendance
commitResults.messageBody:
Present and absent cannot distinguish late arrivals or excused absences.

Extend the existing attendance categories, counts, warnings, and help.
Keep the distinctions through storage, CSV export, correction and undo,
and cover legacy data, batch failures, rollback and UI refresh in tests.

The functional diff is 35 additions and 17 deletions, below the course
feature-freeze allowance even when both sides are counted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify batch student ID validation order
commitResults.messageBody:
Batch commands validate ID formats before checking group membership,
which differs from the UG promise to report the first ID of either kind.

Document the existing validation stages for attendance, participation,
and submission commands while retaining their all-or-nothing guarantee.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct Ravi's grade in the UG listing example
commitResults.messageBody:
The preceding grading example records Ravi as submitted with grade 75,
but the subsequent listing still describes him as not submitted.

Align both the narrative and sample output with the existing grading
behavior so readers can follow the examples consistently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct student counts in DG manual tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The walkthrough adds A3 when testing duplicate-name warnings but later
expects only two students and an empty roster.

Account for all three students and delete A3 before checking the empty
roster so correct application behavior matches the test instructions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a sequence diagram of command confirmation
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG describes in prose how MainWindow asks Logic for a prompt before
executing a destructive command, but has no diagram of it. The flow
crosses UI and Logic and parses the input twice, which is hard to follow
from the text alone.

Let's add a sequence diagram of student delete to the student commands
section. One command is enough, as group delete and assignment delete
follow the same flow. The diagram leaves out the Model to stay focused
on the confirmation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify the confirmation sequence diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The diagram has a ConfirmationHandler column, which exists only so that
tests can replace the dialog. At its width, the page shrinks the diagram
to 84%, so its text is smaller than the course's DG tips recommend.

Let's show the dialog as a step of MainWindow and shorten the notes,
which brings the diagram to 96%. The DG mentions the handler, as the
diagram is a simplified view.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enlarge the TAssist model diagram in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG shows the 1812-pixel model class diagram at a width of 600, so
its text is smaller than the main text and its type parameter box is
hard to read.

Let's show it at 770, the width of the page's content. Rendering it
again is not an option, as a render without Graphviz makes its labels
collide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #313 from arav31/confirmation-sequence-diagram
commitResults.messageBody: Add a confirmation diagram and enlarge the model diagram

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep Records listing after renaming its assignment
commitResults.messageBody:
Renaming an assignment whose records are on the Records screen
replaces the listing with "Assignment PS1 does not exist ... Or create
it with: assignment add a/PS1", which suggests the records are gone.
A listing that cannot be refreshed, such as after switching to a group
without that assignment, shows the same raw error.

Let's move the listing to the new name after a rename, and explain
that a listing is no longer available instead of showing the raw
error with its advice to create the assignment again.

Fixes #315

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject extra words after id/ in student find
commitResults.messageBody:
Student IDs cannot contain spaces, so "student find id/A1 extra" can
only be a typing mistake, yet it searches for "A1 extra" and reports
that no student matches. Other commands reject such extra text.

Let's report the extra text, as the other commands do.

Fixes #316

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the student for invalid week keys in data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A week key that is not a whole number, such as "3.0", is reported as a
JSON syntax error, and a repeated week such as "1" and "01" is
reported without its group or student. The User Guide promises that
these errors name the group and student.

Let's check week keys when converting each student, so that the error
names the group and student like other invalid weekly records.

Fixes #317

commitResults.messageTitle: Show usage when assignment delete or rename lacks input
commitResults.messageBody:
Every other command adds its usage to a missing-parameter error, but
assignment delete and assignment rename only name the missing prefix.

Let's add the usage to these errors too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update version number to V1.6
DG: Describe the Records screen and built-ins accurately
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI component section says records have no screen of their own,
while the same section lists RecordListPanel as one of four screens.
The participation and attendance sections say listings stay in the
feedback box, the built-in command lists omit undo and redo, and the
user stories, UC06 and glossary miss features and terms the DG uses.

Let's describe Records as it works, including how a listing follows
an assignment rename, and fill in the missing stories and terms.

Fixes #319

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Fix activation bars and storage class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
ActiveGroupSequenceDiagram keeps TAssist active between two separate
calls, and self-calls have activation bars in some sequence diagrams
but not in others. The storage class diagram omits
GroupRecordsCsvExporter and the dependency on Model that the text
below it describes.

Let's end each activation where its call returns, give every
self-call its own bar, and add the missing class and dependency.
The PNG images need to be rendered again from these sources.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify help text and parameter error wording
commitResults.messageBody:
Error and help text say "slash particles", which users do not know,
and "Include each exactly once" for missing parameters even when the
missing prefix is id/, which some commands accept many times. Help
text reads "Student is also accepted", as if the capitalized word
must be typed, and the submit and grade entries leave out that s/no
clears a grade and that grades are whole numbers.

Let's name s/o, d/o, a/l and a/p directly, drop the inaccurate
"exactly once", and complete the help entries.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore accents when finding and sorting students
commitResults.messageBody:
A TA who types "jose" does not find José, because the search compares
accented letters exactly, and sorting by name puts Émile after Zoe.
Typing names without accents is common, so both get in the way.

Let's ignore accents in name searches, and sort names alphabetically
so that accented letters sit with their plain letters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the guides and screenshots to match the product
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG screenshots show no Records screen, the Records screenshot says
listings must be refreshed by hand, and several examples fail or
quote other output when typed in the guide's order. Some sections use
jargon, render raw markdown, omit details such as f/ values and the
"..." notation, or keep a long Caution paragraph and a one-question
FAQ.

Let's retake the screenshots, correct the examples and quoted
messages, add an attendance error table and FAQ entries, and describe
accent-insensitive find and sort in both guides.

Fixes #318

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the missing prefix in student command errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Every command names the prefixes it is missing, except the student
commands, which only say "Missing required parameter" before their
usage. The TA then has to compare the input with the format.

Let's name the missing prefixes for student commands too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep page keys and Records refresh in place
commitResults.messageBody:
PageDown past the end of Records or the feedback keeps adding to the
scroll position, so PageUp then seems to do nothing. A four-line
feedback, which shows in full, still takes the page keys away from
Records. Every refresh after a change jumps Records back to the top,
and the student ID column cuts off valid 20-character IDs.

Let's stop scrolling at the end of the text, send the page keys to
Records whenever the whole feedback is visible, keep the position
when a listing is rerun, and let the ID column grow to fit 20
characters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep student search after undoing a group rename
commitResults.messageBody:
Renaming the active group keeps the student search and sort, but
undoing or redoing that rename clears them, because the restored
active group has another name and looks like a different group.

Let's treat a restored active group whose old and new names are each
missing from the other data as the same group under another name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the invalid ID among several student IDs
commitResults.messageBody:
attendance mark, participation set and assignment submit accept many
IDs, but an invalid one gives only "Invalid student ID", so the TA
must check every ID typed. An unknown ID is already named.

Let's name the invalid ID when several IDs are given.

commitResults.messageTitle: Locate invalid group and assignment data in errors
commitResults.messageBody:
An invalid group name, assignment name or assignment record in the
data file is reported without saying which group, assignment or
record holds it, while student errors name the group and student.

Let's name the group, and the assignment or the position of the
record, in these errors too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep save warnings in the terminal to one line
commitResults.messageBody:
A read-only home folder makes TAssist print a Java stack trace of
17 lines in the terminal when it saves preferences, which alarms a
user who glances at it. The UG already explains this case.

Let's log only the reason.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the deleted student's ID and accept view record
commitResults.messageBody:
Names are not unique, yet student delete reports only the name, so
after f/yes nothing confirms which student was removed. view also
accepts the singular student but not record.

Let's include the student ID in the delete feedback and accept the
singular record as well.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop suggesting to create an assignment being deleted
commitResults.messageBody:
Deleting or renaming an assignment that does not exist suggests
"Or create it with: assignment add", which makes no sense when the
TA wants to remove or rename it.

Let's keep that suggestion for the commands that record or list an
assignment, and leave it out for delete and rename.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match curly and straight apostrophes in names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names pasted from documents often contain a curly apostrophe, as in
O’Brien. A search typed with a straight apostrophe does not find
them, and the same-name warning misses O'Brien and O’Brien.

Let's treat both apostrophes as the same when finding students and
when checking for the same name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use singular and plural nouns in counts
commitResults.messageBody:
Search, sort and group deletion report counts such as "1 matching
student(s)", while the Students heading and export already say
"1 student" or "2 students".

Let's share one helper for counted nouns and use it in every count.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say Recorded for a first submission status
commitResults.messageBody:
assignment submit reports "Updated ... to submitted" even when it
records a student's status for the first time, while attendance,
participation and grades say "Recorded" in that case.

Let's say "Recorded ... as" for submission statuses too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Follow assignment renames on undo and in other groups
commitResults.messageBody:
Records loses a listing after undoing the rename it followed, and
does not follow a rename when the listing came from another group
whose assignment has other capitals.

Let's keep the listed assignment's stored name after each refresh,
match renames ignoring case, and follow the last rename back when
undo or redo restores the other name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort student names word by word
commitResults.messageBody:
Sorting by name ignores spaces, so "Tanaka Yuki" lands between
"Tan Ah Kow" and "Tan Bee Lin", splitting students who share a
surname. The DG also describes the old way week-key errors were
reported.

Let's compare names one word at a time, and describe how week-key
errors now name the student.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Explain the apostrophe added to some exported names
commitResults.messageBody:
A name that starts with -, +, = or @ gets a leading apostrophe in the
exported CSV to stop spreadsheets from treating it as a formula, but
the UG does not say so, and some spreadsheets show the apostrophe.

Let's describe this in the export section.
